title: Developer Integration Playbook: Objective-Driven Starter Kits & Support Fix Matrix
author: Arielle Tan
body:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates DX-first starter kits, objective-oriented quickstarts, canonical API examples, docs-site operating rules, and a prioritized support-fix matrix. It is intended for SDK owners, docs authors, solutions engineers, and on-call support engineers who ship or operate integration paths for Redwood Inference.

Goals:
- Reduce first-time integration time (target: < 45 minutes for a basic generation flow).
- Surface a small set of canonical fixes for top support cases so on-call engineers can triage to resolution in under 60 minutes.
- Ensure docs snippets and SDK templates are testable via the docs preview pipeline.
- Keep starter kits objective-driven (business outcome focused) rather than feature lists.

When to use this playbook:
- Building a new SDK adapter or example application.
- Authoring a quickstart for a new model / deployment mode (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Rolling out a docs-site change that includes runnable snippets or a new starter kit.
- When a support ticket matches a known canonical failure pattern.

What we mean by "Objective-Driven Starter Kit":
A small repository or template that maps directly from a customer objective to the minimal set of steps, configuration, and code required to validate that objective. Example objectives: "generate personalized email subject lines from product data", "embed search index and run a semantic search demo", "latency-sensitive chat with streaming responses and function calls."

Starter Kit Catalog (recommended templates):
1) gen-email-subjects-starter (Node + Python): minimal prompt bundling + prefix caching example.
2) embeddings-search-demo (Go + JS): embedding ingest, vector index, basic reranking.
3) streaming-chat-tooling (Python async): streaming responses + function/tool calling example with graceful resume.
4) local-fallback-proxy (Node): showing local caching, rate-limit fallback to hosted API.

Each starter kit must include the following files (template contract):
- README.md (objective, what success looks like, cost estimate)
- quickstart.sh or quickstart.ps1 (one-command bootstrap)
- config.sample.yaml (clearly documented minimal config and environment variables)
- pre-recorded example inputs (in /examples/) and a short test that validates the happy path
- LICENSE and CONTRIBUTING guidance

Example config.sample.yaml:
| key | description | example |
|-----|-------------|---------|
| REDWOOD_API_KEY | API key with developer scope | redwood_test_key_abc123 |
| MODEL_ID | Model to call for the demo | redwood/small-gen-1 |
| BATCH_SIZE | Local batching for requests | 8 |

Quickstart (developer flow) - numbered steps:
1. Clone starter kit: git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/starter-templates.git --depth=1
2. Copy config: cp config.sample.yaml config.yaml and set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env or ci secrets.
3. Run bootstrap (one-command): ./quickstart.sh --bootstrap
4. Execute the basic scenario: ./quickstart.sh --run-smoke and confirm example output in /examples/output.json
5. Open the preview environment: docs-preview URL printed by bootstrap (see Docs Site section below)

Canonical API example (curl + minimal SDK parity):
- curl example (text generation):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/fast-gen-1","input":"Write a subject line for an email about a 20% discount","max_tokens":16}'

- Python SDK parity (requests example):
  import requests
  r = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate",
                    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']}"},
                    json={"model":"redwood/fast-gen-1","input":"Summarize product features in one sentence","max_tokens":20})
  print(r.json())

Docs site operating procedures (docs-team + DX owners):
- Branch naming: dx/<kit>-<short-desc> (e.g., dx/streaming-chat-fix).
- Snippet validation: every PR that modifies code snippets or templates must include a preview build. Previews are gated by the CI job `docs:preview`.
- Preview environment artifacts: link to live snippet runner, generated smoke output, and CI logs. PRs must include at least one successful smoke test run.
- Snippet formatting: use fenced blocks with language tag. Avoid inline secrets; use placeholders like $REDWOOD_API_KEY.
- Release procedure for templates: increment the template manifest version in /templates/manifest.yaml and add a short changelog entry.

Support triage and canonical fixes matrix (top issues):
| Symptom | Likely root cause | Quick triage steps | Canonical fix | Owner | Time-to-fix SLO |
|---------|-------------------|---------------------|---------------|-------|------------------|
| 401 / auth failed | Bad or expired key, wrong scope | Check key env, reproduce with curl; validate scope in billing console | Rotate key or reissue with correct scope; update docs for env setup | customer-success + eng-dx | 60 min |
| Stream disconnects / truncated responses | Client-side streaming buffer/timeouts or gateway idle timeout | Check SDK logs for stream errors; reproduce with small payload; try non-stream mode | Increase client read timeout; enable streaming keep-alive; patch SDK back-pressure handling | eng-developer-experience | 2 hours |
| Token-exhaustion / short completions | Model token limits or unexpected input size | Inspect input size, prefix caching misconfigured | Add input truncation step, enable prefix caching, recommend smaller context model | eng-serving-runtime + eng-dx | 4 hours |
| Rate-limit 429 under burst | Missing client-side rate limiter, or tenant hitting capacity | Check headers (Retry-After); run load trace | Implement jittered exponential backoff; add local token-bucket rate limiter; update quickstart to include client-side backoff snippet | eng-developer-experience | 2 hours |
| Wrong JSON/structured output | Model drift or prompt drift, aggressive temperature | Re-run with deterministic settings, run eval prompt set | Ship a revised prompt template and add a golden test to the starter kit CI | applied-ml-and-evals | 8 hours |

Operational ownership and SLOs for starter kits:
- Each template must have an owner in the CODEOWNERS file at the template root (team + individual).
- On-call for starter-kit regressions: eng-dx rotation. Primary response SLA: 60 minutes for triage, 8 hours for a remediation plan.
- Docs CI metrics: preview build success rate should be > 95% for the main branch.

Rollout checklist for a new starter kit:
1. Author kit using the template contract above.
2. Add unit smoke tests and CI job `template:smoke`.
3. Open PR against docs repo with preview and at least one reviewer from eng-dx.
4. Validation window: run the kit on both hosted API and a local fallback (if included).
5. Merge and update /templates/manifest.yaml with changelog.

Contributor guidance (short):
- Keep examples minimal: prefer a single end-to-end happy path.
- Include cost guidance and a token estimate for the smoke run.
- Add one golden test that fails if output shape changes (structured outputs).
- When changing API surface in examples, update both curl and SDK snippet parity sections.

Escalation flow for unknown failures:
1. Triage on-call (eng-dx) reproduces with curl and the starter-kit smoke test.
2. If reproduction shows platform error, escalate to eng-sre with logs and request-id headers.
3. If model-quality regression, notify applied-ml-and-evals and attach prompt set + example failure.
4. Customer-impacting issues: notify customer-success and follow the customer escalation playbook.

Appendix: Useful commands and snippets
- Run local smoke test (POSIX):
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=redwood_test_key ./quickstart.sh --run-smoke | tee smoke.log

- Minimal token count estimator (bash):
  echo "$(cat examples/input.txt | wc -w) tokens approx"

- Example CI job snippet (yaml):
  jobs:
    template:smoke:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        - name: Setup Python
          uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        - name: Install deps
          run: pip install -r requirements.txt
        - name: Run smoke
          env:
            REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}
          run: ./quickstart.sh --run-smoke
